frequency_question: How often does the U.S. executive branch execute secondary sanctions against major systemic foreign banks for prohibited trade within the specified window?
membership_rule: Includes instances involving G20 or near-peer adversary state financial institutions where primary sanctions frameworks existed; excludes minor boutique banks in pariah states (e.g., North Korea, early Iran phases) where systemic blowback was negligible.

coverage_note: 4 named hits; 3 structural misses where capability existed but executive restraint was exercised (e.g., waivers or diplomatic deferrals on major Chinese banks during prior Iran/Russia compliance enforcement windows).
known_gaps: Excludes classified or purely private diplomatic deterrals that did not reach formal Treasury designation or waiver announcement.
skeleton: Defined class of major geopolitical adversary systemic banking sectors facing structural secondary sanction triggers over major prohibited trade vectors across four presidential administrations.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 7 major confrontation cycles where capability existed (Russia/China systemic trade friction episodes since 2014)
validity_reason: Tied to the stability of the current statutory framework and great-power economic statecraft doctrines; expires with the next structural shift in U.S. executive branch trade weaponization policy.
